title: Build the durable page-level detection/remediation state-tracking artifact
objective: Build scripts/pipeline/lib/reconciliation_store.py, modeled on taskcard_store.py's locking/append discipline (FileLock from advisory_lock.py) but batch-oriented for ~20k-file sweep runs: ReconciliationStore.append_batch(records) / .read_latest() / .read_latest_for_product(family, platform), writing newline-delimited JSON to reports/package-reconciliation/inventory.jsonl (last-occurrence-per-path wins on read). Schema per row: path, family, platform, site, locale, representation (literal|shortcode_block|shortcode_inline|shortcode_maven|mixed|none), registry_type, published, collision_classification, finding_count_literal, finding_count_install_recipe_fail, sweep_run_id, base_sha, recorded_at. Add validate_reconciliation_record() to scripts/pipeline/lib/schema_validators.py.
why_it_matters: No state currently persists between detection and remediation -- every session re-derives scope from scratch, which is the primary reason 16 completed taskcards produced only ~68 of ~6,522 fixes. This artifact is the resumable work queue future sessions and automation read instead of re-discovering scope. Deliberately placed under reports/, not data/package_registry.json -- per-page granularity cannot fit that file's per-(family,platform) shape, and this mission's own plan-repair review already flagged that observation-only fields in data/ risk daily spurious full-portfolio rebuilds once the deploy-trigger fix lands. See governing plan section R.3.1.

title: Narrow the literal-mention detection regex to drop non-Aspose noise (validate before landing)
objective: In scripts/pipeline/audit/package_install_literal.py's verify_package_install_literals(), suppress a structural _INSTALL_CMD_RE match only when the captured token neither contains 'aspose' (case-insensitive) nor is empty/flag-shaped (starts with '-', e.g. '-r requirements.txt', '--upgrade'). Do NOT require exact candidate-identity match -- stay identity-agnostic for anything plausibly Aspose-related, since a hand-typed WRONG Aspose package name is exactly the defect class this gate must keep catching (3D-NET-REFRESH-002 precedent). This is explicitly a lower-confidence item: before landing, run the narrowed rule against a real snapshot of the current ~6,454 findings, manually spot-check a sample (50-100) of everything that disappears to confirm each is genuinely unrelated, and pin regression fixtures for both true positives (cells/net's real collision, the 3D-NET-REFRESH-002 shape) and the named false positives.
why_it_matters: The current regex is deliberately identity-agnostic (correct, by design) but as a side effect matches many commands with zero connection to any Aspose package (pip install -r requirements.txt, pip install --upgrade, pip install fastmcp, pip install markitdown-aspose-cells-plugin) -- 'zero findings' is not a well-defined, achievable target until this noise is characterized and removed. See governing plan section R.3.7/R.1 point 5. Confidence on the exact effect size is explicitly low until validated -- this card's own acceptance checks require that validation before merge, not after.

title: Close the grading-invisibility gap for install_recipe's two safety-critical checks
objective: Split install_recipe.py's shared category='IR' so _verify_publish_channel_claims gets 'IR_PUBLISH_CLAIM' and _verify_no_unpublished_disclosure gets 'IR_UNPUBLISHED_DISCLOSURE' (leave _verify_install_accuracy's 'IR' unchanged). Add SAFETY_OVERRIDE_FINDINGS: frozenset[tuple[str,str]] to content_eval/config.py covering exactly those two (evaluator, category) pairs. Add both new categories to grade_config.yaml's critical_categories. Write a new GRADE_CONTRACT.md section 10 ('Safety-Override Findings') documenting this as a lighter process than full graduation (FAIL-only, deterministic, already-tested, documented safety justification, maintainer sign-off, contract version bump -- explicitly no 14-day wait or corpus-wide noise-rate run, since those bars are about an evaluator's overall noise profile, not two already-verified FAIL-only checks). Bump EVALUATOR_LOGIC_VERSION/EVALUATOR_FREEZE_VERSION, run a full --skip-graded corpus re-evaluation, and record the resulting grade-distribution shift before merging. CONCURRENCY DESIGN JUDGMENT (the independent-review question this child card exists to answer): read advisory_lock.py's FileLock in full. Its mutual exclusion is a real OS-level atomic primitive (`os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY)`), not a Python-level in-process lock (e.g. threading.Lock) -- CPython releases the GIL around blocking os-level syscalls, so two threads racing this open() call genuinely race at the OS/filesystem layer exactly as two separate processes would; the GIL does not mask this class of race the way it would a pure-Python read-modify-write. The test_two_threads_appending_never_corrupts_the_file test is therefore a real proof of the actual mutual-exclusion mechanism, not a fake/serial test dressed up as concurrent -- it starts both threads before joining either, both threads contend for the same lock file, and the assertion (50/50 rows, every line independently valid JSON) would fail under real interleaving if the lock did not work. It is, however, thread-only, not separate-process concurrency -- a real, named scope limit, not glossed over here.

Precedent check: grepped scripts/pipeline/tests/test_advisory_lock.py (the shared lock primitive's own test suite) and scripts/pipeline/tests/test_taskcard_store.py -- NEITHER contains any multiprocessing-based test anywhere in this codebase for this exact lock primitive; both established, already-CLOSED consumers (advisory_lock.py's own test_concurrent_writers_no_lost_updates, taskcard_store.py's own concurrency tests) use the identical thread-based pattern. This taskcard's test is consistent with, not a shortcut below, this codebase's existing accepted bar for this primitive.

Real-usage check: grepped for non-test callers of ReconciliationStore -- locale_patch.py, refresh_knowledge.py, install_defect_sweep.py, reconcile_content_healing_status.py, install_change_budget.py. Read .github/workflows/install-literal-sweep.yml (the one scheduled consumer, currently disabled per MT066 plan B0 decision 3): a single `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` job, not a parallel matrix -- no current production caller spawns literal separate OS processes writing to this store concurrently. Verdict: the thread-only proof is a real, acceptable, precedent-consistent choice for this codebase's actual usage pattern, not a materially weaker claim in practice -- CLOSED, not REWORK_REQUIRED. Flagging for the record (not a blocker): if a future consumer runs this store from genuinely parallel OS processes (e.g. a matrix workflow), a multiprocessing-based regression test would be worth adding then, matching the same bar the rest of the codebase would need to raise for advisory_lock.py generally.

REAL DEFECT FOUND (confirmed by direct code reading, not hypothetical): fetch_file_at_ref() (lines 172-188) and list_path_commits() (lines 199-224) both collapse EVERY non-zero gh api return code -- a legitimate 404/no-data response, but ALSO rate-limiting (HTTP 403), auth expiry, network failure, 5xx, or gh not being installed (FileNotFoundError, also caught and silently swallowed) -- into the exact same 'no data for this revision' / 'no more pages' signal. verify_sha()/classify_sha() have no way to distinguish 'genuinely no scan cycle exists yet' from 'gh api call failed mid-poll', so a rate-limited or errored poll silently returns verdict=PENDING (exit code 0, the same 'nothing to worry about' exit code as CONFIRMED_DEPLOYED/RECOVERED_VIA_LATER_CYCLE) with a message text that is actively misleading about the true cause ('No scan cycle diff range covers this SHA yet -- either too recent, or newer than the sibling repo most recently recorded scan'). No test in the 21-test suite exercises a non-zero/errored gh response for this path (the only nonzero-exit-code tests in the suite, test_file_issue_reports_failure_on_nonzero_exit, cover the SEPARATE file_issue() path, which does correctly report action=failed for its own gh calls). This defeats the tool core purpose exactly in the failure mode most correlated with a real problem: an operator or CI job reading exit code 0 / verdict PENDING has no way to tell a genuine 'too new to judge yet' from 'the check silently failed to check anything.' Recommended fix: distinguish a definitive absence (e.g. HTTP 404 specifically) from any other non-zero/exception outcome, and surface the latter as a loud, distinct failure (non-zero exit, e.g. 3, with a clear stderr message) rather than folding it into PENDING.

SECONDARY MINOR FINDING (same root cause class, lower severity): classify_sha() also mislabels a SHA that predates ALL of the sibling repo tracked scan history (i.e. is itself an ancestor of even the earliest tracked cycle previous_sha) as PENDING with the message 'too recent' -- backwards framing for a SHA that is actually too OLD to be covered by tracked history, though the exit code (0) stays on the safe/non-blocking side so this is cosmetic/misleading rather than dangerous.

file_issue() judged ACCEPTABLE as-is (not a blocking gap): its gh CLI invocation shape (gh issue create --repo <repo> --title <title> --body <body> --label <label>) is real, correct syntax, verified by reading both the code (lines 504-527) and the mocked test (test_file_issue_creates_for_dropped_verdict) which asserts args[:3]==['gh','issue','create'] and --repo targeting. format_issue_body() (lines 477-501) itself is never directly asserted for content in any test (a minor, non-blocking test-coverage gap, not a functional defect on manual read -- straightforward string interpolation with no undefined-variable or control-flow risk), and the exception path (TimeoutExpired/FileNotFoundError) is likewise untested but mirrors the already-tested nonzero-exit failure branch. Given no real SILENTLY_DROPPED case currently exists to test end-to-end against (independently confirmed true), this narrower gap does not by itself warrant REWORK_REQUIRED.
Overall verdict driver: the gh-api-error-silently-becomes-PENDING defect above, not the file_issue() coverage gap, is why this row is REWORK_REQUIRED rather than CLOSED.
rollback_or_recovery: No code changed by this review. Recommended remediation for the cited defect: add an explicit error-vs-no-data distinction in fetch_file_at_ref()/list_path_commits() (e.g. inspect the gh api HTTP status via --include or a separate error-checking call) and thread a loud failure signal through verify_sha() to main() with a distinct non-zero exit code, rather than folding API failures into PENDING.

No partial-write path exists between probe and abort in any of the three sites, a budget-exceeding proposal aborts with zero files touched, confirmed both by direct code tracing and by the passing test_probe_pass_never_writes_before_budget_check and test_dry_run_writes_nothing tests, which assert byte-identical file content after a blocked run.

Verdict: CLOSED. No design or implementation defect found in scripts/pipeline/lib/install_change_budget.py or its 3 real integration sites. title: Fix verify_deploy_trigger.py: distinguish gh api poll failure from genuine no-data (closes TC-PKG-04-L3-REVIEW REWORK_REQUIRED)
objective: Fix the confirmed defect from independent review (TC-PKG-04-L3-REVIEW): fetch_file_at_ref() and list_path_commits() collapsed every non-zero gh api return code (genuine 404, but also rate-limiting, auth failure, network error, timeout, 5xx, or gh missing / FileNotFoundError) into the identical 'no data' signal, so verify_sha()/classify_sha() could not tell a genuinely-nothing-yet poll from a failed poll -- a broken poll silently produced verdict=PENDING/exit 0, the same 'all clear' signal as CONFIRMED_DEPLOYED. Also fix the secondary finding: a SHA predating all tracked scan history was mislabeled with a backwards 'too recent' message.
why_it_matters: This tool is the sole mechanism closing the silent-deploy-drop confirmation gap for data/package_registry.json-only commits; before this fix, the exact failure mode most correlated with a real incident (the gh api poll itself failing) was silently indistinguishable from a clean result, defeating the tool's purpose without anyone noticing.
acceptance_checks: A real HTTP 404 from gh api (confirmed live via its own 'gh: <message> (HTTP <status>)' stderr format) still returns None ('no data') from fetch_file_at_ref() -- regression-checked.

Every other gh api failure (rate-limit/403, auth/401, 5xx, network error with no HTTP status, timeout, gh binary missing/FileNotFoundError) now raises the new DeployTriggerAPIError from fetch_file_at_ref()/list_path_commits() instead of silently returning None/[].

verify_sha() lets DeployTriggerAPIError propagate (does not catch/swallow it); main() catches it and exits 3 (EXIT_API_POLL_FAILURE) -- distinct from exit 0 (clean verdict) and exit 2 (pre-existing bad-SHA lookup error, unchanged).
Secondary finding: a SHA that is an ancestor of the EARLIEST tracked cycle's own previous_sha now gets a corrected 'predates tracked history' message; verdict/exit code unchanged (still PENDING/0).
pytest scripts/ci/tests/test_verify_deploy_trigger.py -q -- all tests green, including the pre-existing 21 (no regression) and 19 new tests for this gap.
check_monkeypatch_lint.py --strict --tier 1,2 on both changed files -- clean.
Live CLI re-run against the 3 previously-verified real SHAs -- byte-for-byte same verdicts as both the implementer's and the reviewer's prior claims.
evidence_refs: Commit b16d987b1ae971678c276f3290458cdeb689ed80 (pushed to origin/main via git_plumb_commit.py, skill S-99 pipeline-harden, scoped to scripts/ci/checks/verify_deploy_trigger.py and scripts/ci/tests/test_verify_deploy_trigger.py): fix(ci): verify_deploy_trigger.py -- distinguish gh api poll failure from genuine no-data (TC-PKG-04-L3-FIX). 2 files changed, 463 insertions(+), 24 deletions(-).

New class DeployTriggerAPIError + _gh_http_status() helper (scripts/ci/checks/verify_deploy_trigger.py); fetch_file_at_ref() and list_path_commits() now raise it for any non-404 gh api failure; verify_sha() propagates; main() gained EXIT_OK=0/EXIT_DROPPED=1/EXIT_LOOKUP_ERROR=2/EXIT_API_POLL_FAILURE=3 constants and a try/except DeployTriggerAPIError branch returning EXIT_API_POLL_FAILURE; main() also gained a keyword-only `runner` testing seam (mirrors every other function in the module) threaded to sha_exists_locally/verify_sha/file_issue.

classify_sha() secondary-finding fix: when native_cycle is None and cycles is non-empty, checks whether the SHA is an ancestor of cycles[0].previous_sha (predates all tracked history) and returns a corrected message instead of the generic 'too recent' one; verdict/exit code unchanged.

Confirmed live (2026-09-17) via direct `gh api` calls against a nonexistent path and a nonexistent ref in Aspose/aspose.org-workflows that gh's real failure stderr format is exactly 'gh: <message> (HTTP <status>)' (e.g. 'gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)') -- basis for the _gh_http_status() regex.

title: Narrow the literal-mention detection regex to drop non-Aspose noise (validate before landing)
objective: In scripts/pipeline/audit/package_install_literal.py's verify_package_install_literals(), suppress a structural _INSTALL_CMD_RE match only when the captured token neither contains 'aspose' (case-insensitive) nor is empty/flag-shaped (starts with '-', e.g. '-r requirements.txt', '--upgrade'). Do NOT require exact candidate-identity match -- stay identity-agnostic for anything plausibly Aspose-related, since a hand-typed WRONG Aspose package name is exactly the defect class this gate must keep catching (3D-NET-REFRESH-002 precedent). This is explicitly a lower-confidence item: before landing, run the narrowed rule against a real snapshot of the current ~6,454 findings, manually spot-check a sample (50-100) of everything that disappears to confirm each is genuinely unrelated, and pin regression fixtures for both true positives (cells/net's real collision, the 3D-NET-REFRESH-002 shape) and the named false positives.
why_it_matters: The current regex is deliberately identity-agnostic (correct, by design) but as a side effect matches many commands with zero connection to any Aspose package (pip install -r requirements.txt, pip install --upgrade, pip install fastmcp, pip install markitdown-aspose-cells-plugin) -- 'zero findings' is not a well-defined, achievable target until this noise is characterized and removed. VERDICT: REWORK_REQUIRED. title: Fix install_defect_sweep.py's reconciliation-store writer so locale_patch.is_english_source_ready() can ever pass through the reviewed sweep pipeline
objective: Root-cause fix (not another workaround) for the 3-times-independently-confirmed gap: install_defect_sweep.py's writer only ever wrote a product-level aggregate reconciliation row at a synthetic path (reports/audit/install-defect-sweep/{family}-{platform}), never a real per-file row keyed the way locale_patch.is_english_source_ready() looks it up -- so the readiness gate could never pass through the normal, reviewed sweep pipeline for any product, for any file, ever.
evidence_refs: Read is_english_source_ready() (scripts/pipeline/commands/content/locale_patch.py:202-221): keys its lookup by _reconciliation_key(source_path) -- the repo-root-relative, forward-slash content path -- via store.read_latest().get(key); refuses (fail-closed) when no row exists, when representation=='literal', or when collision_classification=='COLLISION_RISK_STRUCTURAL'.

Read install_defect_sweep.py's _reconciliation_rows() (pre-fix): confirmed independently (not just trusted from the 3 finding agents' reports) that it builds exactly one row per (family, platform) at path f'reports/audit/install-defect-sweep/{family}-{platform}' -- never a content/ path. Confirmed via test_install_defect_sweep.py's own pre-existing TestReconciliationRows fixture, which only ever exercises the aggregate shape.

Read reconciliation_store.py's append_batch()/schema (schema_validators.validate_reconciliation_record): required fields path/family/platform/site/locale/representation/sweep_run_id/recorded_at; representation in {literal, shortcode_block, shortcode_inline, shortcode_maven, mixed, none}; collision_classification in {SAFE_FOR_MECHANICAL_MIGRATION, COLLISION_RISK_STRUCTURAL, COLLISION_RISK_PENDING_VERIFICATION, NOT_APPLICABLE, None}.

Implemented _english_source_file_rows() in install_defect_sweep.py: emits one real per-file row per ENGLISH-SOURCE content file the literal sweep scans (locale=='en', via the same _locale_from_path() package_install_migrator.py/locale_patch.py already use), with representation/finding_count_literal computed per-file via the same verify_package_install_literals() call the aggregate sweep already uses (same convention: representation='literal' if any finding else 'shortcode_block', matching _reconciliation_rows()'s existing rule so aggregate and per-file views stay consistent). Wired into run_combined_sweep() so one sweep run writes BOTH the aggregate and the new per-file rows under the same shared sweep_run_id.

Scale decision (step 8): live dry-run against the real portfolio (install_literal_sweep.run_sweep()) measured total_files_checked=20956, total_files_with_findings=3938, total_findings=5288 in 14.25s. A second live pass computed English-source-only (locale=='en') file counts: total_en_files=918 (4.4% of corpus), en_with_findings=21, non_en_with_findings=3917 -- confirming almost all real findings are locale-lag defects in non-English copies, and that is_english_source_ready() (which only ever looks up the English source) never needs a row for those 3917 non-English files. Chose to scope per-file row emission to English-source files only (918/sweep), not the full 20956-file corpus, based on these real counts, not a guess.

Benchmarked reconciliation_store.append_batch()/read_latest() directly (scratch script, not committed): 918-row batch = 6.7ms write / 3.5ms read_latest; 20956-row batch = 99.2ms write / 75.2ms read_latest; after simulating 10 cumulative weekly sweeps at the 918-row scope, read_latest stayed at 94.5ms over ~30k lines / 9.3MB. Both scopes are technically fast per-call, but the store has no compaction/pruning path anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by grep across every ReconciliationStore consumer) -- a full-corpus weekly emission would add ~21000 rows/week unboundedly (~1.09M rows, ~350MB/year at 322 bytes/row), versus ~918 rows/week (~48k rows, ~15MB/year) for the English-source-only scope -- about 23x smaller for zero loss of coverage on the one lookup shape is_english_source_ready() ever performs.

Also confirmed a real, positive side effect (not additional scope): reconcile_content_healing_status.py's compute_transition() reads read_latest_for_product() and sums finding_count_literal across every row for a product; adding real per-file rows cannot flip its any-nonzero-blocks decision (aggregate and per-file rows agree whenever findings are nonzero, and English-source-clean rows always contribute 0), and its own 25-test suite (test_reconcile_content_healing_status.py) still passes unmodified.

title: Watcher re-resolves unpublished package identity every run; one observation per package per run; hardened fetch; adapter fault isolation
objective: package_publish_watch.check_unpublished_entries re-resolves identity (naming convention, then the registry's own search, platform-compatible and corroborated) whenever an unpublished entry's STORED name is definitively absent, and treats an empty candidate as resolvable instead of skipping it forever. A per-run snapshot wrapper makes the publish, version-update and drift checks evaluate ONE observation per package, memoizes search per family, and converts an adapter exception into an ambiguous result for that entry only. package_registries.default_fetch gains one bounded retry on transport faults and 429/5xx and maps http.client.HTTPException to ambiguous; the NuGet net/cpp platform-compatibility rule becomes a single shared function used by both registry_backfill and the watcher. apply_proposal records identity_basis when identity was re-resolved.
why_it_matters: Proven live 2026-09-18: NuGet Aspose.Slides.Cpp.FOSS 26.9.0 (published 2026-09-14, authored by Aspose, project URL = the slides FOSS cpp repo) could NEVER be detected because backfill froze the CMake name aspose_slides_foss on 2026-08-01 and the watcher only ever re-probed that frozen guess. Also proven: each published entry was sampled twice per run (two independent observations feeding two counters), one malformed response aborted the whole run, and api.nuget.org connect stalls (~2-3 of 50 calls) each cost the debounce a full scheduled day.
acceptance_checks: slides/cpp at counter 1 against the real NuGet adapter, via run_auto_apply on a scratch copy: proposes and applies candidate Aspose.Slides.Cpp.FOSS, published true, validate_package_registry returns no errors
each published entry is sampled exactly once per run; a second run samples again
ambiguous alternate probe holds the counter; nothing found anywhere resets it exactly as before
unrelated commercial package (PyPI aspose-page) and a Cpp package for a net entry are never adopted
pytest over every test file importing a changed module -> 914 passed, 7 skipped
rollback_or_recovery: git revert the commit. No registry or content data is written by this change; the watcher's persisted state format is unchanged apart from an optional identity_basis value the validator already allowed.

title: _parse_dotnet_manifest must identify the library package, not a shallower executable/tool that also declares a PackageId
objective: In extraction/package_manifest.py rank executables (OutputType Exe/WinExe, PackAsTool) below libraries when choosing which csproj declares the package, enumerate deterministically (sorted before the cap, cap raised to 200) and read each csproj once.
why_it_matters: 3d/net declares two PackageIds: the CLI src/converter/Converter.csproj (OutputType Exe, Aspose.3D.Converter, depth 3) and the real library (Aspose.3D.FOSS, depth 4). The shallowest-PackageId rule picked the tool, so the knowledge model and through it the published docs taught readers to install Aspose.3D.Converter, which returns 404 on NuGet; it also fed net10.0 only as the target framework instead of the library's net10.0/net8.0/net6.0/netcoreapp3.1.
acceptance_checks: old (git HEAD) vs new extractor over all 7 .NET clones in the clone cache: only aspose_3d_net changes (Aspose.3D.Converter 1.0.0 -> Aspose.3D.FOSS 26.1.0, target frameworks corrected); the other 6 identical
5 new tests fail against the old code and pass against the new; cap-before-sort test places the real project at both ends of the alphabet so it does not pass by enumeration luck
pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/extraction + test_scout_extraction.py -> 531 passed
rollback_or_recovery: git revert the commit. Knowledge artifacts are not regenerated by this change; 3d/net knowledge/install.md keeps its stale Converter identity until a re-scout runs (see PKGINSTALL-KNOWLEDGE-USES-REGISTRY-IDENTITY).

objective: test_all_31_launched_products_are_registered now asserts every data/products.json product has a registry entry (derived, non-vacuous); test_slides_net_is_confirmed_not_published becomes test_slides_net_identity_and_verification_are_coherent (pins the hand-verified identity and the published->evidence_url invariant, not a point-in-time external fact); test_real_repo_scan_matches_manual_audit asserts coverage (uncovered_pairs empty, registered >= discovered) instead of a hardcoded 32.

title: Move watcher control-plane state (debounce counters, timestamps, ambiguity streaks) out of the Hugo-consumed data/package_registry.json
objective: Keep data/package_registry.json as the Hugo contract that changes only on public-visible transitions (published flips, identity, maven/cargo version). Persist observation state in a separate store that is neither under data/ nor gated behind a human-merged PR (a dedicated state branch or workflow artifact), so counters advance every run regardless of PR merge timing. Add wall-clock separation to the debounce (first_seen_at) and an ambiguity-streak alert. Deploy-trigger Layer 2 (PKGINSTALL-DEPLOY-TRIGGER-3LAYER-FIX) MUST NOT land before this: mapping data/ in detect_changes.py while counters live in that file would rebuild four sites on every counter-only PR.
why_it_matters: Proven 2026-09-18: (1) MT066 acceptance criterion 'no debounce counters in a Hugo-consumed data/ file' is violated by the existing fields consecutive_checks_agreeing / consecutive_version_checks_agreeing / consecutive_checks_absent; (2) the watcher checks out main, so an unmerged daily PR rewinds counters and page/python cannot reach 2 without a human merge between two runs; (3) two runs seconds apart satisfy the 2-consecutive-check debounce, so it counts runs not elapsed time; (4) persistent ambiguity is silent.
acceptance_checks: a counter-only run produces no diff in data/package_registry.json
counters advance across runs with an unmerged registry PR open
two runs within the minimum interval do not satisfy the debounce
cross-repo: the deployed workflow in Aspose/aspose.org-workflows persists the new state store (operator-approved change)
rollback_or_recovery: Feature-flag the state location; reverting restores counters in the registry file with no data loss.

override token created and consumed for the layouts/shortcodes edit

title: The install-literal migrators must only rewrite a literal that names the registry candidate package
objective: Make package_install_migrator.py and package_install_inline_migrator.py (and the locale_patch propagation path) refuse, and report, any literal whose package token is not the registry candidate for that family/platform, with TDD. Today they rewrite any pip/npm/dotnet/go install literal in a product's pages into that product's shortcode, so a literal naming a DIFFERENT package would be silently replaced by the wrong install command.
evidence_refs: Found by the TC-PKG-02-13 lane (page/python): in all 24 kb troubleshooting.md files the stock inline migrator would have rewritten a literal install of fastmcp, a different package, into the aspose-page-foss shortcode; the lane had to anchor the kb, products and protected-page migrations on the registry package by hand (5 commits 55d58f7a1e, ffda7af065, 1ef2f2f092, 5151bd9d05, ede9c40472). The 45 remaining fastmcp literals are correct as literals and are not sweep findings.

Same class seen three times in this mission, each time handled by hand by the lane: cells/python (a markitdown plugin package under its own heading; the block migrator ce57cf1754 from 2026-08-01 already turned that literal into the cells/python shortcode, so 37 pages render the wrong command today, card TC-PKG-03-08), 3d/python and 3d/net (locale rows naming the commercial packages aspose-3d and Aspose.3D, cards TC-PKG-03-04 and TC-PKG-03-09), and page/python (fastmcp).

Acceptance: red-first tests where a literal naming a non-candidate package is left untouched and reported with its file and line, for the block migrator, the inline migrator and locale_patch; existing migrator tests stay green; a dry-run over page/python, cells/python and 3d/python reports the known non-candidate literals instead of migrating them. Scripts under scripts/pipeline/commands/content/ have no registered skill: use gap-escalation scoped to the files. Independent review before closing.
